On agent-created cards, I would draw the boundary at agreed scope. An agent can create a linked subtask or open question needed to complete an already accepted task, with a brief explanation of why it is necessary. New goals or optional improvements should remain proposals until a human accepts them. Creating a card should never automatically assign work to someone else or change priorities. That keeps routine decomposition moving while leaving control of scope with the team.

I would also use a flag for vague, duplicated, or stale cards instead of a Smells column: a task can be in progress and still need attention. Flags surface issues immediately; a short weekly review gives us a regular opportunity to resolve flags that remain unanswered.
